Job Description
Aviation Environmental and Egress Technicians maintain and repair aircraft systems such as: ejection seats, crash worthy seats, utility systems,
furnishings, and canopy systems; maintain gaseous and Liquid Oxygen (LOX) and nitrogen systems and Environmental Control Systems (ECS)
and subsystems; maintain ordnance and manage explosive devices (i.e., Cartridge Actuated Devices (CAD) and Propellant Actuated Devices
(PAD) etc.); configure aircraft for flight schedules; manage scheduled and unscheduled maintenance; and perform daily, pre-flight, post-flight,
conditional and other periodic aircraft inspections.

Aviation Structural Mechanics (Safety Equipment) (AME) maintain ejection seats, canopy jettison components, and environmental control, fire extinguishing, and associated life support systems; maintain gaseous and liquid oxygen, cockpit/cabin pressurization, heating and cooling, and ventilation systems, and avionics cooling, and anti-gravity components; maintain utility systems and associated lines, fittings, valves, control mechanisms, oxygen gauges, converters, and regulators; inspect, remove, and install ejection seats and associated components; inspect, remove, and install explosive devices; rig and adjust canopy assemblies; operate and maintain Liquid Oxygen (LOX), gaseous oxygen and nitrogen systems, and Support Equipment (SE); and perform daily, pre-flight, post-flight, conditional and other periodic aircraft inspections. __________________________________________

Aviation Environmental and Egress Technicians maintain and repair aircraft systems such as: ejection seats, crash worthy seats, utility systems, furnishings, and canopy systems; maintain gaseous and Liquid Oxygen (LOX) and nitrogen systems and Environmental Control Systems (ECS) and subsystems; maintain ordnance and manage explosive devices (i.e., Cartridge Actuated Devices (CAD) and Propellant Actuated Devices (PAD) etc.); configure aircraft for flight schedules; manage scheduled and unscheduled maintenance; and perform daily, pre-flight, post-flight, conditional and other periodic aircraft inspections.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
